main_text.p: tûs pars est non minima. الحجر الاسود Alhajar al aswad, i. e. Lapidem nigrum vocant. At unde illi nomen Bracthan? num forsan quasi براقة Barracaton, à برق Coruscare, Fulgere, quia cùm primò è Paradiso (ut fabulantur demissus fit, كان اشد بياضا من الثلج وبضي كما قضي الشمس, i. e. Candore nivem superabat, & splendore solem aquabat, ut loquitur Ahmed Ebn Yusef? qui factum ut

p.i: Qui color albus erat nunc fit contrarius albo

main_text.p: mox dicetur. At certè crediderim Bracthan nomen lapidis non fuisse, sed qui eâ voce usus fuerit, rationem reddere voluisse, cur lapidem istum oscularentur, eique adhærerent, scil. ut inde درکة Baracatan, i. e. benedictionem consequerentur, osculantur eum siquidem تبركابه Tabarracan behi, boni omninis, seu benedictionis captanda gratiâ. Nam ut asserit Safiod-dinus ما زال هذا الحجر معظما في الجاهلية والاسلام. يتبركك الناس به ومروا دوده ويقبلونه, i. e. Non defiit lapis iste in magno honore esse & olim ante Mohammedis tempora, & post immutatam ab eo cultûs rationem tatabarrao olnas behi, i. benedictionem ab eo captabant homines, sub eo transfire, eúmque venerabundi osculari. Erit ergò lapis τὸ Βαί[?] la-pis Benedictionis, seu quem benedictionis consequendæ gratiâ osculantur. Ut intelligantur quæ tam de lapide isto, quam de Oratorio adduntur, de utroque paucis erit dicendum. Quod ad ἀποσωτήριον[?], illud est quod الكعبة Alcaaba, Caabam vel κάαβα (ut efferunt Graeci) vocant, nomine vel ab eminentia indito, quia scil. quicquid eminet & excelsum est كعب

page.notes: <note side="left">In vita Ada-mi.</note> Note: the Arabic and Greek words are transcribed from the scan and may contain small errors; the Greek word after "lapis" (τὸ Βαί[?]) and the Greek word after "Quod ad" (ἀποσωτήριον[?]) are doubtful. "mox dicetur" is read as "mox", the first letter being uncertain on the scan. The left-margin note's hyphenation ("Ada-mi") is uncertain; a dot-like mark may stand for the hyphen. The printed hyphen in "la-pis" is a soft break and is not printed; "la-pis" is printed as one word across the line and is written here as "lapis". Line "Safiod-dinus" retains its printed hyphen at the line end.
